rationale: B wins because it keeps three real stories and knows exactly where the proof gates are. A's "Allbirds Quietly Dropped 'Eco-Friendly' as Its Main Pitch" is a confident leap from one durability claim into a whole brand-repositioning thesis. B's "Allbirds' comeback shoe comes with a durability claim. Where's the test data?" turns the same fact into a usable product/materials angle without swallowing the company's marketing whole.
gaps_in_A: "Allbirds Quietly Dropped 'Eco-Friendly' as Its Main Pitch" asserts a marketing pivot the update does not prove; the fact block only says the new platform is described as more durable.
"For a Brand Built on Cutting Out Middlemen" imports D2C identity and anti-wholesale positioning that are not in the supplied facts.
"Is That the Template for D2C Brands That Survived?" needs outside comparables; the update gives Allbirds' cuts, not a category-wide pattern.
The next step says the durability and wholesale angles are "ready to draft once the partner name is confirmed," but the durability angle still needs test data and marketing-copy evidence.
gaps_in_B: "shrinks its way to a first margin gain" nudges causality; the facts show cuts and margin improvement, not that the cuts caused the margin gain.
"committing floor space" and "shelf space" assume an in-store wholesale relationship; the update only says a named retail wholesale partnership.
"customer-story" is the wrong label for a wholesale-partner perspective; this is a trade/channel angle, not a real customer case study.
"A news-peg angle — none built" is sloppy wording because the margin report and relaunch are current pegs; what is missing is an external newsjack peg.
